questions.q: What does right-sizing an EC2 instance mean?
options: Matching the instance's size to its actual observed CPU and memory usage
Always choosing the largest instance type available
Renaming the instance to match its tag
Moving the instance to a different AWS Region
questions.explain: Right-sizing replaces a launch-time guess with an instance size that matches what the workload actually uses, based on real utilization data.

questions.q: Which CloudWatch metric is the key signal for identifying a right-sizing candidate?
options: CPUUtilization (and memory usage) averaged over time
The number of IAM users in the account
The instance's launch timestamp
The number of security groups attached
questions.explain: An instance that consistently shows low CPU and memory utilization over a couple of weeks is a strong candidate to downsize.

questions.q: Why do unattached EBS volumes cost money even though nothing uses them?
options: EBS volumes bill by the gigabyte-month regardless of whether they're attached to a running instance
AWS automatically deletes them for free after 30 days
They only cost money while an instance is attached
Unattached volumes are always free of charge
questions.explain: A volume left in the 'available' (unattached) state keeps billing until it's manually deleted, even if its original instance was terminated long ago.

questions.q: What does an S3 lifecycle policy do?
options: Automatically transitions objects to cheaper storage classes, or deletes them, as they age
Automatically increases the price of an S3 bucket over time
Prevents any object in the bucket from ever being deleted
Converts S3 objects into EBS volumes
questions.explain: A lifecycle rule can move aging objects from Standard to Standard-IA, then Glacier, then Glacier Deep Archive, and delete them after a retention period.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, why is the m5.xlarge web server a good right-sizing candidate?
options: CloudWatch shows average CPU under 8% and memory under 30%, even at peak traffic
It has been running for exactly one year
It uses S3 Glacier for storage
It has more than one security group attached
questions.explain: Consistently low CPU and memory utilization, even at peak, means the instance is over-provisioned and a smaller instance type would handle the same load.
